  pdf_document: default
  html_document: default
---

```{r}
data(mtcars)
head(mtcars)

# PCA is affected by the scale of the variables, so standardization is usually necessary.
mtcars_scaled <- scale(mtcars)
pca_mtcars <- prcomp(mtcars_scaled, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE) # you can also scale the data here.
summary(pca_mtcars)
# Standard deviation; Proportion of variance explained; Cumulative variance explained
pca_mtcars$rotation
# loading matrix


# Scree Plot: helps decide how many PCs to keep
library(factoextra)
fviz_eig(pca_mtcars)

# Biplot Visualization
library(ggbiplot)
ggbiplot(pca_mtcars)

# PC1 captures the direction of maximum variance.
# Each PC is a linear combination of the original variables.
# The biplot shows both data points and variable loadings — useful for seeing relationships between variables and identifying clusters.
```
